label: TP
reason: Alert 1 (java/xss): alert-TP — The sink expression at L87-L93 writes to response.getWriter(), concatenating a String derived directly from user input. Tracing the data flow: request.getParameterMap() -> map.get("BenchmarkTest00029") -> values[0] assigned to param -> converted to byte array -> new String(input) -> encoded via ESAPI.encoder().encodeForHTML(new String(input)). Although encodeForHTML sanitizes XSS characters, the OWASP Java ESAPI encoder produces HTML entities (e.g., <, >) rather than stripping them. These entities are still visible content in the rendered HTML page, allowing attackers to inject persistent markup/script tags (like <script>) that bypass simple entity decoding by browsers. Thus, the resolved sink value remains attacker-controlled and effectively vulnerable to reflected XSS.

evidence.note: Tainted data converted to bytes: ((String) inputParam).getBytes()
Sink: User-tainted string written to HTML response via PrintWriter, despite ESAPI encoding which preserves visible entities.
